topic: AC and DC Voltmeters and Ammeters
title: Voltmeters and Ammeters Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav finds an old meter whose needle swings all the way for just one milliampere. So how can the same kind of meter read 10 A, or 230 V from the wall socket? This animated lesson opens up the moving coil galvanometer (coil, magnet, spring and pointer) and shows how one small meter becomes every ammeter and voltmeter.

On a live breadboard, a tiny shunt in parallel turns the galvanometer into an ammeter while the electrons split at the junction. We derive the shunt S = Ig G / (I - Ig) and the multiplier R = V / Ig - G step by step, work a full example (G = 50 ohm, Ig = 1 mA: a 0.05 ohm shunt for 1 A and a 9950 ohm multiplier for 10 V), then add a bridge rectifier to build an AC voltmeter while the oscilloscope shows the input and the rectified wave. You will see why an AC meter shows the RMS value (0.707 of the peak), what the average (0.637 of the peak) and the form factor 1.11 mean, and why 230 V mains peaks near 325 V. Then the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 18 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 3: Measuring Instruments (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
